body.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\), the explicit local-polynomial learners satisfy \(\mathsf G_n\). In particular, \(\mathfrak B_n=O_P(n^{-2\beta}\log n)\) and therefore \(n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n=O_P\{n^{5/6-2\beta}(\log n)^{5/2}\}=o_P(1)\) because \(\beta>5/12\); bounded foldwise empirical increments give \(\sqrt{\log n}\,\mathfrak R_n=o_P(1)\); and the smooth plug-in estimates give \((\log n)\mathfrak K_n=o_P(1)\) and \(|\widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)-1|=o_P(1)\). More generally, whenever \(\mathsf G_n\) holds and \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), optimized-value stability gives \(\{S_n-S_n^{\circ}\}/a(T_n(P))=o_P(1)\) uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\).
body.justification: This separates the actual product, local empirical, variance-normalization, and clock thresholds required at the moving Gumbel level from the stronger instrumental assumptions used to verify them.
body.gap: Published pointwise causal-isotonic LR theory requires a nuisance product small relative to one cube-root neighborhood; the displayed conditions add the logarithmic accuracy needed after scanning order \(n^{1/3}\) dependent neighborhoods.
body.consumer: Three remainder clauses are algebraically supported; the centered V-statistic term and optimized-value stability remain prerequisites for implementation.

obligation.what_is_open: The fold-conditional centered local empirical bound and the implication from the four numerical remainders to optimized constrained-versus-unconstrained LR stability remain unproved.
obligation.obstruction: Within-fold marginalization makes the perturbation a validation-fold V-statistic, while optimized-value comparison additionally needs common contact localization and slope envelopes not included in the four clauses of \(\mathsf G_n\).
obligation.attempted: The product-bias, variance plug-in, and volume plug-in orders were proved; a direct objective comparison stops at uncontrolled integration-by-parts boundary and total-variation terms.
obligation.partial_result:
Conditional on the bounds displayed in \(\texttt{lem:learner-rates}\), the product term obeys
\[
\mathfrak B_n=O_P(n^{-2\beta}\log n),
\]
and therefore
\[
n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n
=O_P\!\left(n^{5/6-2\beta}(\log n)^{5/2}\right)=o_P(1),
\qquad
\frac56-2\beta=-\frac16+\frac{d+1}{2s}<0.
\]
On the event where stabilization gives fixed positive lower and upper density bounds, product, quotient, and integration inequalities also give
\[
\mathfrak K_n=O_P(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}),
\]
and
\[
\left|\frac{\widehat{\mathcal V}_n}{\mathcal V(P)}-1\right|
=O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n}
+n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right).
\]
These calculations verify the product-bias, variance-normalization, and spatial-clock clauses of \(\mathsf G_n\) once the learner bounds are available.  They do not verify the centered local empirical clause because the validation-fold marginalization inside \(Z_i\) is a fold-conditional V-statistic.  Nor do the four scalar clauses alone provide common contact localization and slope envelopes for the constrained and unconstrained isotonic projections, which are required to compare their optimized objective values.
